answer: Limit simultaneous contracts by locked collateral rather than account count. A pigment buyer escrows payment, while each seller locks a bond until delivery and the dispute window end. The same bond cannot back a lantern order and a sonnet commission at once, even through different keys; the ledger tracks unspent collateral. A swarm promising a thousand jobs must fund a thousand bonds, with failed delivery forfeiting each bond to the affected buyer. This limits cheap mass fraud, not fake names, and requires fair dispute rulings and affordable bond sizes.
